verdict.tagline: Master water physics and build sprawling beaver settlements.
for_you_if: you enjoy open-ended sandbox city builders
you want deep water management mechanics
you need a game that runs well on older hardware
not_for_you_if: you require structured campaigns and definitive endgame goals
you prefer comprehensive tutorials for complex systems
you push hardware limits with massive settlements

citations.review_text: 100% would recommend, though make sure you’re not trying to play on something super old
this game is one of the best games i played. It runs well on low settings

claims.claim: Reviewers highlight water management mechanics such as building dams, reservoirs, and handling droughts and bad tides as central gameplay features.

citations.review_text: If you loved Banished, Timberborn takes that classic survival city-builder formula and gives it an awesome twist with sentient beavers and complex water physics. Your main challenge isn't just feeding your furry citizens, but mastering hydrology building dams, floodgates, and reservoirs to store water for drinking and farming before disaster strikes. You’ll constantly be tested by brutal Droughts that dry up the river and Bad Tides that flood your land with toxic sludge, forcing you to think fast to protect your colony. Overall, it’s a super satisfying, highly replayable game that delivers 15 to 40 hours of pure fun as you watch your mega dam projects successfully hold off the apocalypse!

As someone who doesn't usually enjoy these types of games, Timberborn is pretty great, very simple to understand but with enough depth that it constantly makes you think. There's droughts that hit pretty hard at times, cutting off all the water in the map, along with bad water surges that will kill every if they get near your growing areas. So you're constantly managing how to store water and redirect water around the map. I just started digging into automation and it's very cool, I've never played an automation game before so it's a learning process though.

The water mechanics alone make this a worthwhile pick up. Lots of care and attention to detail in this one for strategy fans. figuring out how to dam half the map and turn it into your pool is a blast.

Only played two days, but I can easily see why this game consistently has Overwhelmingly Positive reviews. It scratches the itch that city-management-gamers love. Plays similar to the feel of Banished and Dawn of Man, but perfected what the mechanics. Everything feels intuitive, easy to understand and the tutorial is well done. I love the management of toxic waste flow vs. fresh water, and you get to do what beavers do best, build dams and control that flow, which then instantly transforms the usable terrain. I just think it's all done very well, and not over-complicated. This may be the best game I played this year. I was glad to see it on sale!

claims.claim: Reviewers note the absence of an endgame goal, scenario wins, or campaign objectives, leaving players to build and expand freely without a definitive finish state.

citations.review_text: There are no objectives or missions or scenario win. You just play until you lose or get bored. The technology tree is more about perpetually grinding than actually achieving anything.

Sorely disappointing for a 1.0

There's no endgame goal to strive for and once you solve the only real difficult threat (which you aren't warned about before it happens, the tutorial seems half-baked) there's not much to do other than build and expand. And while I get that for a city builder, some end-state would have been preferable so I can move on to another map/difficulty/beaver type. Building for building's sake is a lazy copout by developers.

The gameplay itself is pretty basic, not challenging, and gets old quick. No events, no lore, just - build and expand until you get bored. I have no idea how this is so highly rated, it's entirely overpriced for what you get.

cohorts.summary: Players note that core mechanics require independent experimentation because tutorials lack depth.

claims.claim: Reviewers note that the tutorial lacks depth or leaves out explanations for core mechanics like badwater and stairs, requiring players to figure things out on their own.

citations.review_text: Fantastic game.  Needs much better tutorial, in-game guide.  This is a situation where early development meant a base that understood the game very well.  But they never created an easy way to fully understand what's going on . Tutorial stops before other stuff is really needed.  Had no clue whatsoever how to deal with Badwater.  How to do stairs, etc.

Not much hand holding or details on mechanics, but I really like that. Lots to find out on  your own and fun things you can do. I really like all the water mechanics and frustrating at times beaver things (no spoilers). First game in a while that's got me hooked like this.
Tutorial could be better, but overall a good sandbox game you will enjoy for many hours.

cohorts.label: 100h+
cohorts.summary: Long-term players encounter performance drops when constructing massive settlements and complex water systems.

claims.claim: The game suffers from performance drops, frame rate issues, and stuttering when building large settlements with hundreds of beavers or complex water systems.

citations.review_text:
I love everything about this game except... medium to large cities are NOT optimized to run well and it does not seem to matter how beefy your computer is. I have a city with 1500 beavers and even with all the graphics turned all the way down, the game engine struggles to keep the framerate above 15. The physics engine is not using all cores on my processor and not using the GPU to it's max either and the game is grinding to a halt, VERY often freezing or stuttering so bad it becomes a slideshow and I have not even built on 2/3 of the map yet. 

This PC is fairly new and certainly no slouch; I can play other AAA titles at almost max settings and not run into performance issues like what Timberborn has caused so far and I have not even modded the game yet. I am not overheating, there are no other apps running, and every setting which could be altered to try to fix performance issues has been entertained to no avail.

VERY disappointing, and I will keep playing, but it looks like my flagship beaver city needs to be abandoned, along with any hope of completing any of the large or medium maps the game offers. :/

I only recommend this game in the scope that you need to have a VERY beefy computer, expect low framerates with a beaver population over 300, and expect to be limited on how big and fancy your city and it's districts will be, regardless of if you have a bleeding edge setup.

For me personally, this game could have been the perfect city builder if it weren't for its terrible optimization. As soon as you build a medium-sized settlement with 200–300 beavers and a relatively complex water system, the game just starts stuttering like crazy all the time. What's the point of making a city builder that can't even handle a moderately medium settlement, let alone mega-projects? This game simply doesn't make sense. Disappointing.
Very fun. Aesthetically pleasing. Challenging at times. Great game, highly recommend. If they could figure out the autosave stutter it would be perfect.

This game had a pleasant cycle of boom and bust. Multiple resources must be balanced and spun. It's plenty cute, and yet a ruthless city builder. By my 500th beaver the cityscape had filled the map and my computer had slowed to a crawl. God it was worth it.
